description: The pie chart, titled in the context of “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the distribution of media bias categories across 100 total cases, with each slice labeled by category, percentage, and raw count. The largest segment, colored blue, corresponds to “Right bias,” accounting for 30.0% (30 cases). The second-largest, in orange, is “Left bias” at 28.0% (28 cases). A green segment labeled “Questionable source” comprises 22.0% (22 cases), while the smallest red slice, “20.0% (20),” appears unlabeled in the chart but is likely intended to represent another category such as “Neutral” or “Unbiased,” though its label is missing. A gray legend box is present to the right of the chart but contains no text or key, rendering it non-functional. The slices are arranged clockwise starting from the top-right, with no apparent exploded or emphasized segments, and percentage values are displayed inside each slice alongside their integer counts in parentheses.
